# FreezerTest knowledge base

Version: **0.2 — owner review, first batch** · Updated: **27 October 2026**

This knowledge base explains the FreezerTest apparatus, control software, test sequence, data, and analysis methodology. It is intended for operators, colleagues, and a local AI answering questions about the test. It describes a particular source snapshot, not a certified operating procedure or a validated hardware inventory.

The original code review covered **33 shared Python/shell files**, identical to GitHub commit `df4ccebbbd0f41e32f5ae415e967728e5845d56b` (12 October 2026), plus the local configuration. Three project chats supplied historical context. The owner's **27 October review** adds component identities, operating corrections, and six filter-wheel CAD files, and supersedes conflicting historical assumptions. Details still awaiting confirmation are kept in one [review register](09-review-questions-and-gaps.md). See [sources and maintenance](10-sources-and-maintenance.md) for provenance.

## Find information

| Document | Use it for |
|---|---|
| [01 — Purpose and system overview](01-purpose-and-system-overview.md) | What is measured, system diagram, vocabulary, and scope |
| [02 — Hardware and connections](02-hardware-and-connections.md) | Components, digital I/O, temperature probes, filter wheel, and camera interfaces |
| [03 — Software and configuration](03-software-and-configuration.md) | Modules, dependencies, deployment, defaults, and local overrides |
| [04 — Running the test](04-running-the-test.md) | Pre-cool, measurement, sweeps, repeats, stopping, and recovery |
| [05 — Data and metadata](05-data-and-metadata.md) | Folder structure, files, metadata, timestamps, and transfer |
| [06 — Analysis methodology](06-analysis-methodology.md) | Spectral and spatial metrics, signal/noise, ROIs, units, and limitations |
| [07 — Analysis tools and troubleshooting](07-analysis-tools-and-troubleshooting.md) | Analysis commands, comparisons, preview tools, and common problems |
| [08 — Project context and owner review](08-project-context.md) | Camera-family scope, confirmed context, and relevant historical distinctions |
| [09 — Review questions and gaps](09-review-questions-and-gaps.md) | Prioritized questions for our review, including missing hardware details |
| [10 — Sources and maintenance](10-sources-and-maintenance.md) | Evidence, exact source version, history coverage, and update procedure |
| [11 — Using this with a local AI](11-local-ai-guide.md) | Import options, answer rules, and retrieval checks |
| [12 — Glossary](12-glossary.md) | Terminology used in the code and documentation |

## Evidence labels

- **Implemented / source-derived:** visible behavior in the reviewed code. This does not prove the deployed camera has the same files.
- **Configured:** a value in the reviewed configuration. Local overrides take precedence where the consuming module uses the value. A setting's presence alone does not implement a feature.
- **Owner-reported:** a physical detail or observation stated by the owner in a retrieved project chat; historical and subject to review.
- **Proposed / unverified:** an earlier suggestion, an interpretation, or a feature not established by the reviewed sources.
- **Unknown:** evidence is missing. These gaps are deliberately left open.

## Read these distinctions first

1. **Normal pre-cool ends at `probe_5 <= 5 °C`.** The 12 °C setting in the historical copied profile was intentional for a shorter trial. The probe's physical location still needs confirmation. Neither threshold establishes thermal equilibrium of the whole camera.
2. The test covers **Qtec Hypervision variants**, both to establish reproducibility across units and to investigate design changes. There is no single fixed reference-camera revision. Record the unit, revision, focus/setup, and run settings for meaningful comparisons.
3. The measurement phase uses the chamber's warm-up after cooling. No closed-loop heater ramp or temperature stability hold is implemented in the reviewed runner.
4. Analysis widths and shifts are in **pixels**. Signal and image-noise metrics are in **digital numbers (DN)**. The code does not establish calibrated spectral resolution in nm, temporal read noise, or acceptance limits.
5. Preflight and diagnostic scripts can switch real outputs. They are not all read-only checks. Do not run them alongside an acquisition.

## Scope and delivery

Individual runs, images, measured performance, camera rankings, and causal conclusions about camera development are excluded. Setup-related failure modes and measurement validity concerns are retained. The root `calibration_temperature_log.jsonl` and compiled `__pycache__` files are not part of the knowledge corpus.

The numbered Markdown files are the editable source of truth. `exports/FreezerTest_Knowledge_Base.md` is a single-file copy for import. `exports/documents.jsonl` provides one record per document, and `exports/chunks.jsonl` provides section-level records. Import **one representation only**, so the local AI does not retrieve duplicate copies. [The local AI guide](11-local-ai-guide.md) explains the details.

The first review batch replaces answered gaps and removes the abandoned warm-start procedure from active guidance. Its unused variables have been removed from the local configuration; the original configuration snapshot remains historical evidence. No acquisition program was run, no camera files were deployed, and no historical analysis was rerun. The [CAD reference](reference/filterwheel-cad/README.md) and labeled preview are part of the documentation, outside the scripts-only test-PC checkout.

# Purpose and system overview

Status: owner review, first batch · Updated: 27 October 2026 · Code snapshot reviewed: 23 October 2026

## What FreezerTest does

FreezerTest automates temperature-dependent optical measurements of a camera using a freezer, temperature probes, a switched light source, and a motorized filter wheel. A host PC coordinates the apparatus and asks an embedded Linux camera computer to capture images. Offline analysis extracts image position, line/edge width, signal, and image-noise indicators, then compares their evolution within a test and across repeated tests.

The devices under test are **variants of the Qtec Hypervision camera family**, using Qtec computer logic and hardware. There is no single fixed reference-camera revision: multiple units of the same kind are tested to build evidence of reproducibility, while deliberate camera changes are also tested to investigate their consequences. The method and apparatus belong here; individual outcomes and development decisions remain outside this corpus. [Owner review R1](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026).

Qtec describes Hypervision as an Offner push-broom hyperspectral camera based on its C-series platform. The owner describes the relevant camera range as approximately 400–1700 nm; Qtec's current VIS-SWIR family documentation specifies 430–1700 nm. The exact configuration, detector, optics, and revision should be recorded for each tested unit rather than copied wholesale from a generic product page. See [Qtec Hypervision](https://docs.qtec.com/hsi/hypervision/intro/), [project context](08-project-context.md), and [hardware](02-hardware-and-connections.md).

Primary source: [long-test runner](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L441), [single sweep](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L201), [analysis configuration](../Config/analysis_config.py#L14), and [chat T2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#t2-freezer-camera-drift-analysis).

## Functional architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PC[Host PC: Python orchestration and local data]
    DAQ[Network MCC DAQ: thermocouples and digital I/O]
    TC[Five enabled K-type probe channels]
    HALL[Filter-wheel Hall input]
    RELAYS[Lamp, camera power, freezer control outputs]
    TIC[Tic stepper controller and filter wheel]
    CAM[Embedded Linux camera: V4L2 and GStreamer]
    FILES[Camera staging: PNG and JSON]
    LOCAL[Host test folders: images, logs, metadata]
    ANALYSIS[Offline analysis and comparison tools]
    PC -->|network uldaq| DAQ
    TC --> DAQ
    HALL --> DAQ
    DAQ --> RELAYS
    PC -->|ticcmd interface| TIC
    PC -->|SSH commands| CAM
    CAM --> FILES
    FILES -->|SCP transfer and local checks| LOCAL
    PC --> LOCAL
    LOCAL --> ANALYSIS
```

This is a software-level diagram. The diagram does not establish electrical isolation, relay contact ratings, a shared power-supply topology, or physical component locations. The [hardware page](02-hardware-and-connections.md) distinguishes those unknowns from configured connections.

## Acquisition hierarchy

| Term | Meaning in this project |
|---|---|
| Repeat sequence | A configured number of complete tests, with one shared repeat-group identifier |
| Test / repeat | One test folder containing pre-cool events, temperature logging, a measurement phase, and cleanup |
| Sweep | One ordered visit to all configured filter positions, normally producing four images plus metadata |
| Capture | One image at one filter position; filters are captured sequentially, not simultaneously |
| Analysis row | A per-sweep result assembled from available images, metrics, and associated temperatures |

This distinction matters: a filter-4 image is taken later than the filter-1 image in the same sweep. A sweep-associated temperature is not automatically the exact optical-component temperature at every individual exposure. See [data and metadata](05-data-and-metadata.md).

## Current configured measurement channels

| Wheel position | Analysis name | Intended role | Nominal optical filter setting | Exposure control value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `no_filter` | Spatial edge/line-spread analysis and signal ROIs | Open/no filter according to analysis configuration | 3000 |
| 2 | `bp_780` | Spectral line profile | Thorlabs **FBH780-3**: 780 nm, nominal FWHM 3 nm | 15000 |
| 3 | `bp_1064` | Spectral line profile | Thorlabs **FLH1064-3**: 1064 nm, nominal FWHM 3 nm | 8000 |
| 4 | `bp_1550` | Spectral line profile and background/noise ROIs | Thorlabs **FBH1550-4**: 1550 nm, nominal FWHM 4 nm | 15000 |

The owner selected these narrow bandpass filters to sample widely separated portions of the camera's wavelength range. They provide three discrete spectral samples, not continuous coverage or absolute wavelength calibration. Component identities are owner-confirmed; nominal wavelengths/widths agree with [Thorlabs' specification table](https://www.thorlabs.us/newgrouppage9.cfm?objectgroup_id=16235&pn=FB1070-10). The position-to-analysis mapping comes from [analysis configuration](../Config/analysis_config.py#L14); exposures shown are the historical copied profile, from [local configuration](reference/local_config_snapshot.txt#L58). Per-run filter-position verification remains necessary. Exposure values are passed to `exposure_time_absolute`; their physical unit must be confirmed for the deployed driver. See [camera control](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L50).

## Current implemented test concept

Normal preparation includes verifying filter positions before each long test and manually focusing on the target plane when changing cameras. The runner starts temperature logging, switches lamp and camera off, and runs the freezer until the selected pre-cool threshold is met; the owner-confirmed normal threshold is **`probe_5 <= 5 °C`**. The copied configuration used 12 °C for a shorter trial. A pre-cool timeout aborts the test. On successful pre-cool, the runner switches the freezer off, waits 60 seconds, powers the camera on, waits 45 seconds, and starts keepalive streaming when enabled. It then captures sweeps during warm-up until the selected endpoint logic ends measurement. The historical copied profile ends after three consecutive new records observed at `probe_5 >= 40 °C`, with a 14-hour measurement deadline checked between operations, and requests eight repeats. Blocking operations and the final sweep can extend that deadline. These trial-specific settings should not be treated as universal protocol requirements. [Owner review R1](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026).

The runner does not command a controlled heating rate, establish thermal equilibrium at setpoints, or check humidity. These distinctions are central to interpreting temperature-associated measurements. See [running the test](04-running-the-test.md), [review gaps](09-review-questions-and-gaps.md), and [pre-cool code](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L330).

## What the analysis can answer

- How spectral profile peak positions and FWHM change in image coordinates.
- How the selected spatial edge and its fitted line-spread width change.
- How selected signal-region mean DN and background-region spatial scatter change.
- How those metrics relate to associated external probe temperatures, selected internal camera temperatures, sweep index, and repeat identity. Recorded timestamps support additional time-based analysis, but the supplied viewers do not offer an elapsed-time axis.

The methodology does not, by itself, establish absolute wavelength accuracy, intrinsic spectrometer resolution independently of the bandpass filters, radiometric response, temporal noise, MTF, or a root cause of drift. It does not supply pass/fail specifications. [Analysis methodology](06-analysis-methodology.md) records the exact calculations and limits.

## Boundaries with a future camera-development knowledge base

This corpus keeps apparatus details, operating behavior, analytical definitions, configuration provenance, and known threats to measurement validity. A future camera-development corpus should own individual test outcomes, comparisons between camera units, drift histories, design experiments, proposed root causes, and decisions about optical or mechanical redesign.

The historical camera construction details in [project context](08-project-context.md) are retained only to explain the device under test and to guide the hardware review. Earlier assistant hypotheses about glue, expansion, or mechanical settling are not treated as established facts.

# Hardware and connections

Status: owner review updated 27 October 2026; original source snapshot 23 October 2026. Component identities and arrangement supplied in the [27 October owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026) are distinguished below from software settings and generic manufacturer specifications. This is not yet an as-built wiring drawing. Physical probe locations, remaining part numbers, actual supply wiring and optical geometry still require review.

## System arrangement

The host PC runs the test coordinator, reads an Ethernet MCC temperature/DIO unit, commands a Tic stepper controller, and triggers image capture on the camera computer over SSH. The camera computer exposes a V4L2 video device and saves PNG images before transferring the sweep to the host. The freezer, lamp, and camera power are switched through the MCC digital outputs. The Hall home sensor is read through an MCC digital input. These are software relationships; cable routes and terminal numbers have not been established from a drawing. [Temperature and DIO controller](../Control/temperature_control.py#L69), [filterwheel driver](../Control/filterwheel_control.py#L42), [remote capture](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L51).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Host[Host PC: coordinator and local data]
    MCC[MCC Ethernet temperature and DIO unit]
    Tic[Tic stepper controller]
    Wheel[Filterwheel and stepper motor]
    Camera[Camera computer: V4L2 and GStreamer]
    Probes[K-type thermocouples]
    Hall[Hall home sensor]
    Lamp[Lamp switching circuit]
    Power[Camera power relay]
    Freezer[Freezer contactor]
    Host -->|Network DAQ interface| MCC
    Host -->|ticcmd| Tic
    Tic --> Wheel
    Host -->|SSH and file transfer| Camera
    Probes --> MCC
    Hall -->|AUXPORT0 bit 1| MCC
    MCC -->|AUXPORT0 bit 0| Lamp
    MCC -->|AUXPORT0 bit 2| Power
    MCC -->|AUXPORT0 bit 3| Freezer
```

The diagram is a logical interface map. It does not specify load-side power wiring, isolation, connector pin numbers, or electrical polarity beyond the configured logic levels below.

## Component inventory and evidence

| Component | Established identity, owner description or code interface | Still to confirm physically |
|---|---|---|
| Host PC | Python programs coordinate tests, store data, run analysis and Streamlit comparison views. | Machine identity, operating-system version, interface configuration, environment/package versions, backup location. |
| Camera and embedded computer | Owner identifies the Qtec Hypervision family, with variations tested rather than one fixed hardware revision. SSH control, `/dev/video4`, V4L2 and GStreamer are implemented. | Per-test camera/revision identity, sensor, serial number, firmware/driver versions, optics, TEC hardware and setpoint. |
| MCC temperature and digital-I/O unit | Owner supplies Digilent/MCC **E-TC**, part **6069-410-025**. Ethernet `uldaq` access; eight configured thermocouple channels and `AUXPORT0` bit I/O. | Serial number, terminal map, common/reference connections and calibration status. |
| Thermocouples and extension | Owner supplies **Omega 5SRTC-TT-KI-36-1M** thermocouples and **Labfacility XF-1275-FAR** KX extension wire. Channels 0–4 enabled as type K. | Attachment methods, physical positions, actual extension lengths, connector counterpart model, reference measurements and uncertainty. |
| Tic controller and stepper motor | Owner identifies **Pololu 3132, Tic T834**, and a **NEMA 17** motor. Controlled with `ticcmd`. | Exact motor part number/electrical rating, serials, actual controller supply, winding wiring and mechanical drive ratio. NEMA 17 does not identify a specific motor model. |
| Filterwheel and Hall home sensor | Owner confirms sensor on the fixed base and magnet on the rotating part; supplied datasheet identifies Honeywell **SL353 series**, with HT/LT variants. Four configured measurement positions and active-low Hall logic. Six CAD meshes are preserved below. | Exact HT/LT suffix, fitted supply/interface circuit, physical datum, assembled dimensions and optical alignment. |
| Filters | Owner identifies **Thorlabs FBH780-3**, **FLH1064-3** and **FBH1550-4**, plus the open position. Nominal wavelengths/widths agree with analysis configuration. | Per-unit transmission data/certificates, orientation, installed mounting and serial/lot records. |
| Illumination | Lamp controlled by DIO bit 0; software waits 2 s before sweep capture. | Lamp/source type, spectrum, power supply, warm-up stability, positioning, optical path and switching interface. |
| Freezer and contactor | DIO bit 3 controls freezer enable; automated pre-cool followed by freezer-off measurement. | Freezer model, compressor/controller details, contactor and coil ratings, temperature limits and physical wiring. |
| Camera power relay | DIO bit 2 controls camera power; 45 s boot wait configured. | Relay specification, load-side voltage/current, power-supply topology, switching behavior and actual boot requirement. |
| Camera mounting, grating and target | Analysis expects spectral lines and a central dark vertical line; local notes mention a “PC Grating Holder.” User chat describes an Offner arrangement and the materials listed below. | Complete optical/mechanical drawing, grating properties, target description, distances, orientation and confirmation that the historical build is still current. |

Sources: [camera defaults](../Camera_scripts/camera_config.py#L2), [DAQ interface](../Control/temperature_control.py#L12), [temperature configuration](../Config/temperature_config.py#L8), [system motion and I/O settings](../Config/system_config.py#L1), [filter identities](../Config/analysis_config.py#L12), [target analysis setup](../Config/analysis_config.py#L41), [local metadata](reference/local_config_snapshot.txt#L66).

### Manufacturer specifications and their limits

The owner's camera description is approximately **400–1700 nm**. Qtec's public Hypervision documentation lists its VIS-SWIR version as **430–1700 nm**, describes an Offner spectrograph, and places it on a Linux computer platform. Preserve these as separate owner and public-product descriptions: the public specifications do not establish the exact range, detector or revision of every camera tested here. Record the camera identity for each run, and perform the owner's stated manual focus adjustment when changing camera. [Qtec Hypervision documentation](https://docs.qtec.com/hsi/hypervision/intro/), [owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026).

Digilent identifies **6069-410-025** as **MCC E-TC**, with eight thermocouple inputs, 24-bit conversion, maximum 4 samples/s/channel and eight digital I/O. These are device capabilities, not the project's logging cadence or whole-chain accuracy. The code's logger requests a nominal 1 s interval. [Digilent E-TC product page](https://digilent.com/shop/mcc-e-tc-thermocouple-measurement-ethernet-daq-device/), [logger interval](../Control/temperature_logger.py#L21).

Pololu identifies item **3132** as the **Tic T834 with soldered connectors**, using a DRV8834 driver. Its manufacturer supply range is **2.5–10.8 V**, with approximately **1.5 A continuous per phase** without additional cooling. The actual installed supply voltage remains unrecorded. The separate 24 V camera/contactor comment below does not establish a supply connection to this controller. [Pololu 3132](https://www.pololu.com/product/3132).

## Optical and mechanical setup reported in project chats

In the 31 August 2026 project discussion, the user described an **Offner setup**, with the slit in a steel cup, rods made from **SS304**, and a **polycarbonate (PC) grating holder** intended to provide thermal compensation. The user discussed an approximately four-times-expansion rationale for that design; this is an engineering explanation from the chat, not a validated material property or established athermal performance measurement. The steel-cup grade was not established by the retrieved wording and should not be assumed to be SS304 merely because the rods are. [Project context](08-project-context.md), [retrieved chat source T2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#t2-freezer-camera-drift-analysis).

The same user description identifies an unspecified **Loctite superglue** for the grating and **Casco SuperFix+** for the mirror-to-top-plate bond. Exact Loctite product, bond thickness/geometry, cure conditions, substrate preparation and resulting thermal/mechanical properties are not documented. This is evidence of adhesive choices reported for that build; it does not establish whether a later build changed them. No adhesive material constants have been inferred from product names. [Project context](08-project-context.md), [retrieved chat source T2](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#t2-freezer-camera-drift-analysis).

Other retrieved user discussion reports the freezer fan running during cooling, thermocouples and 24 V wiring, and prior condensation. The available discussion does not establish a complete current fan wiring/control circuit, humidity measurement, or an installed drying solution. Previously proposed condensation remedies are not treated as fitted hardware. See [the retrieved project context](08-project-context.md) for source limits and historical discussion.

## Network and device interfaces

| Connection | Configured value | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Host to camera | Camera endpoint `10.100.10.100`; SSH account selected by `CAMERA_USER` | Noninteractive SSH is used; connection and authentication must already work. No password or key belongs in this knowledge base. |
| Host to MCC | Host `10.100.10.101`, port `54211`, interface `None` | Values passed to `get_net_daq_device_descriptor`; a specific interface is not selected in configuration. |
| Camera video | `/dev/video4` | Shared by PNG capture, keepalive streaming and sensor-temperature refresh by default. |
| Host to Tic | `ticcmd`, with `TIC_SERIAL=None` | No explicit device serial is selected in the current settings. Record the intended controller before using a host with multiple Tic devices. |
| Camera-side program directory | `/root/scripts/` | Capture and camera-temperature programs are expected here. |
| Camera-side image staging | `/root/scripts/data` | Sweeps are stored here before host transfer. |

These are configuration values, not confirmation that the devices are currently reachable. Sources: [camera network and paths](../Config/system_config.py#L82), [MCC endpoint](../Config/temperature_config.py#L8), [Tic device selection](../Control/filterwheel_control.py#L42), [SSH options](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L51).

## Digital input and output map

All four signals use the MCC `DigitalPortType.AUXPORT0`. A bit index is a software channel designation, not a connector pin number. [Port setup](../Control/temperature_control.py#L35).

| Logical function | AUXPORT0 bit | Direction | Active/on state | Inactive/off state | Where set |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| Lamp | 0 | Output | 1 | 0 | Hard-coded in `temperature_control.py` |
| Filterwheel Hall sensor | 1 | Input | 0 | Any value other than 0 evaluates inactive | Configured `HALL_DIO_BIT`, `HALL_ACTIVE_STATE` |
| Camera power relay | 2 | Output | 1 | 0 | Configured camera-power constants |
| Freezer contactor | 3 | Output | 1 | 0 | Configured freezer constants |

The camera and freezer active levels are configurable; their off levels are calculated as the inverse. Connecting the controller turns the lamp and freezer off and configures the camera-power bit as an output. The connection method does **not** explicitly turn camera power off at that point; the pre-cool workflow does this later. Disconnect attempts to turn the lamp, freezer and camera power off. [Connection behavior](../Control/temperature_control.py#L69), [signal read/write functions](../Control/temperature_control.py#L102), [disconnect](../Control/temperature_control.py#L168).

The recorded `lamp_state`, `freezer_state`, and `camera_power_state` represent the program's commanded state. There is no separate feedback measurement in this controller proving that the relay operated, power reached the load, the lamp emitted light, or the compressor ran. [State fields and readings](../Control/temperature_control.py#L199).

### Shared supply and sequencing caveat

A comment in the calibration program states that the freezer contactor uses the camera 24 V supply and that camera and freezer should not be enabled together. That program turns the freezer off before enabling camera power. Treat this as a recorded design constraint requiring confirmation against the actual wiring. The low-level `camera_power_on()` and `freezer_on()` methods do not implement a mutual interlock; the normal long-test pre-cool sequence provides sequencing at a higher level. [Calibration comment and action](../Scripts/calibrate_filterwheel.py#L181), [low-level outputs](../Control/temperature_control.py#L116), [pre-cool sequencing](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L330).

## Thermocouple channels

The owner identifies the thermocouples as **Omega 5SRTC-TT-KI-36-1M**. Omega lists that exact model as type K, **36 AWG / approximately 0.13 mm wire diameter**, **PFA insulation**, and **1 m lead length**; the 5SRTC style includes a miniature thermocouple plug and strain relief. These product details do not establish the physical placement or calibration of any particular probe. [Omega IEC series and exact model listing](https://www.jp.omega.com/pptst/5LSC_5SRTC_IEC.html).

The owner confirms that the thermocouple connectors are **inside the freezer**, extended outside with **Labfacility XF-1275-FAR** KX wire, [Farnell order reference 2918721](https://dk.farnell.com/labfacility/xf-1275-far/thermocouple-wire-type-kx-10m/dp/2918721). This identifies extension wire, not a separate connector product. The exact mating/extension connector model has not yet been supplied; do not infer it from the cable reference or the probe's included plug. Actual installed extension lengths and termination details remain to be recorded. [Owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026).

| MCC channel | Logical probe name | Thermocouple type | Enabled in supplied configuration | Physical placement |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `probe_1` | K | Yes | Unconfirmed |
| 1 | `probe_2` | K | Yes | Unconfirmed |
| 2 | `probe_3` | K | Yes | Unconfirmed |
| 3 | `probe_4` | K | Yes | Unconfirmed |
| 4 | `probe_5` | K | Yes | Unconfirmed; used for current pre-cool and measurement endpoint |
| 5 | `probe_6` | K | No | Unconfirmed |
| 6 | `probe_7` | K | No | Unconfirmed |
| 7 | `probe_8` | K | No | Unconfirmed |

Source: [channel map](../Config/temperature_config.py#L12). Probe names are generic identifiers. Do not label a probe “ambient,” “grating,” “camera housing,” or similar until its actual placement is confirmed.

The owner reports **5 °C at probe 5** as the normal cold threshold and explains that **12 °C** was used recently to shorten testing. The archived local configuration contains 12 °C. These are protocol choices, not probe specifications or verified temperatures of the optics; retain the actual selected threshold with each test. [Owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026), [configuration snapshot](reference/local_config_snapshot.txt#L27).

At connection, the controller sets a thermocouple type for every entry, including disabled channels. During a read it skips disabled channels, asks the device for Celsius values, and records `ULException` errors per probe. It does not apply a project-specific offset or scale correction in this code. Factory/device calibration and cold-junction behavior must be documented from the actual MCC model and its setup rather than inferred here. [Type setup](../Control/temperature_control.py#L77), [temperature reading](../Control/temperature_control.py#L210).

The default logger interval is 1 s, with a sleep after each reading cycle, so this is a nominal cadence rather than a guaranteed exact 1 Hz sample clock. [Logger defaults](../Control/temperature_logger.py#L21), [logger loop](../Control/temperature_logger.py#L79).

## Filterwheel, filters and position calibration

The owner identifies the three installed filter models below. Their nominal center wavelengths and FWHM values agree with the [analysis configuration](../Config/analysis_config.py#L12) and Thorlabs' product descriptions; no individual filter transmission certificate has been supplied. The three narrow passbands sample separated wavelengths across the broad camera range. They do not provide continuous spectral coverage of that range. [Thorlabs filter table](https://www.thorlabs.us/newgrouppage9.cfm?objectgroup_id=16235&pn=FB1070-10), [owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026).

| Filter number | Analysis name and role | Owner-supplied model | Nominal wavelength | Nominal filter FWHM | Archived local position | Base-file position | Capture exposure control value |
|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | `no_filter`, spatial/open | Open position | — | — | -51 | -57 | 3000 |
| 2 | `bp_780`, spectral | [Thorlabs FBH780-3](https://www.thorlabs.com/item/FBH780-3) | 780 nm | 3 nm | -251 | -257 | 15000 |
| 3 | `bp_1064`, spectral | [Thorlabs FLH1064-3](https://www.thorlabs.com/item/FLH1064-3) | 1064 nm | 3 nm | -451 | -457 | 8000 |
| 4 | `bp_1550`, spectral | [Thorlabs FBH1550-4](https://www.thorlabs.com/item/FBH1550-4) | 1550 nm | 4 nm | -651 | -657 | 15000 |

The local positions override the base positions. The owner reports checking filterwheel positions for each long run; the archived numbers are not a permanent alignment guarantee. Values are Tic position units under the configured step mode, not verified angles or absolute physical positions. Adjacent configured slots are separated by 200 position units; no steps-per-revolution or gear ratio is established in the source. Exposure values are passed to the camera driver's `exposure_time_absolute` control. Their time unit and valid range require camera/driver verification; do not convert them into milliseconds using a generic camera convention. [Base positions and motion settings](../Config/system_config.py#L3), [local positions and exposures](reference/local_config_snapshot.txt#L52), [exposure command](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L50), [owner review](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026).

### Mechanical reference and Hall arrangement

The owner confirms that the **Hall sensor is attached to the fixed base** and the **magnet is on the rotating part**. The supplied datasheet is Honeywell's **SL353 series micropower omnipolar digital Hall sensor**, covering **SL353HT** and **SL353LT**. It specifies a **2.2–5.5 V** operating supply, **−40 to +85 °C** operation, and a **push-pull output** that goes low with an activating magnetic field and high when it is removed. That logic agrees with the configured active-low read. Either magnetic pole can activate the device. [Honeywell datasheet supplied via RS, pp. 2–4](https://docs.rs-online.com/9a79/A700000007013601.pdf), [Hall configuration](../Config/system_config.py#L25).

The exact fitted **HT/LT suffix remains unknown**: the nominal sampling periods differ (45 microseconds for HT versus 45 milliseconds for LT at the datasheet's nominal conditions). Record the actual suffix and interface wiring when documenting the homing response; no sensor-response/repeatability validation is inferred from the family datasheet. Its IC pin diagram is not an as-built pin map for the rig.

Six supplied STL files are preserved in the [filterwheel CAD inventory](reference/filterwheel-cad/README.md), with a preview below. The meshes provide mechanical reference; their assembled roles, exact current-build correspondence and dimensions should be established from the inventory and owner review rather than guessed from filenames or this preview.

![Independent views of the six supplied filterwheel CAD meshes](assets/filterwheel-cad-overview.png)

Current coordinator settings are step mode `8`, current limit `1500 mA`, max speed `4000000`, starting speed `0`, max acceleration/deceleration `40000`, position tolerance `5`, settle time `0.2 s`, and move timeout `10 s`. Speed and acceleration numbers are passed directly to `ticcmd`; this knowledge base does not convert their units without the actual controller documentation. Class constructor defaults differ from the coordinator configuration, so use the passed configuration when interpreting production behavior. [Configured values](../Config/system_config.py#L10), [driver constructor](../Control/filterwheel_control.py#L13), [coordinator passes settings](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L241).

The controller is energized for motion, then de-energized at idle and during image capture by default to reduce stepper heating. During homing it stays energized between the search steps. De-energization is an intended thermal behavior; whether the wheel can drift while unpowered must be checked physically. Controller-reported position is not an independent measurement of optical alignment. [Move behavior](../Control/filterwheel_control.py#L119), [homing current behavior](../Control/filterwheel_control.py#L172).

### Hall homing

With the normal configuration, home search direction is `-1`, coarse increment `50`, fine increment `1`, and maximum coarse travel counter `3000`. The algorithm:

1. If Hall is already active, move away until inactive.
2. Search coarsely toward the magnet until Hall becomes active.
3. Move away in fine increments until inactive.
4. Approach in fine increments until the active edge is found, then set Tic position to zero.

The result records the starting, coarse-hit, inactive-edge and final-edge positions plus duration. The 3000 counter limits the initial move-away and coarse-search stages. The fine back-away/approach loops do not have their own travel or elapsed-time bound in this implementation. A successful software home therefore establishes a sensor-edge reference, not an independently measured repeatability specification. [Homing configuration](../Config/system_config.py#L25), [homing implementation](../Control/filterwheel_control.py#L158).

### Calibration workflow supported by the code

`Scripts/calibrate_filterwheel.py` provides `home`, position readout, absolute movement (`g`), relative jog (`j`), move-to-filter (`f`), save-current-position-to-filter (`s`), lamp/camera switching, and a `save` command. A useful documented sequence is to home, identify each optically aligned slot, record the current position for that filter number, save, then transfer the reviewed positions into `Config/local_config.py`.

The calibration program writes `calibrated_filter_positions.json`. The test runner does **not** load that file automatically; it uses `FILTER_POSITIONS` from configuration. The help text mentions filters 1–8, while the supplied running map defines four. The existence of a calibration command for a number does not prove the physical wheel has that many populated slots. [Calibration commands](../Scripts/calibrate_filterwheel.py#L39), [position saving](../Scripts/calibrate_filterwheel.py#L144), [JSON write](../Scripts/calibrate_filterwheel.py#L204), [runtime map use](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L314).

## Camera internal temperature channels and TEC

There are two sources of internal readings:

- `sensors -j` supplies whatever hardware-monitor sensors exist on the camera computer. The program maps driver families to friendly names such as CPU, GPU, FPGA, Sensor PCB and PCB. These names are software labels, not proof that every component exists or is measured at the exact location implied by a label.
- V4L2 supplies `sensor_temperature`; the program treats its integer value as millidegrees Celsius and divides by 1000, then rounds to 0.1 °C. It also reads `temperature_control` and records a Boolean when parseable. It does not set or regulate a TEC setpoint.

Sources: [driver name map](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L22), [hardware-monitor parsing](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L66), [V4L2 conversion and control status](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L277).

The camera-side code states that this camera's sensor-temperature control updates only while video is actively streaming. It therefore keeps a temporary stream alive while reading, or uses the existing keepalive stream. An exactly 20.0 °C camera reading receives a possible-default/stale warning; that is a diagnostic flag, not evidence that all 20 °C readings are invalid. [Refresh rationale](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L152), [warning](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L327).

## Hardware information to add during review

1. Annotated overview photograph, optical-path sketch and a dimensioned mounting arrangement.
2. Per-test camera/revision and serial records; MCC/controller serials; exact NEMA 17 motor model and SL353HT/LT suffix; remaining freezer, lamp, supply, relay and contactor identities/manuals.
3. Wiring drawing with connector/terminal numbers, logic references, supply sharing and load-side switching.
4. Photograph and location description for each `probe_1` through `probe_5`, including what surface or medium it measures and how it is attached.
5. Individual filter transmission certificates/lot records; target description; grating, lens and holder details.
6. Temperature calibration/uncertainty evidence, wheel alignment/repeatability check, illumination stabilization evidence and camera exposure-control units.
7. Confirmed operating temperature bounds and the actual camera/TEC initialization and control behavior.
8. Confirm the historical Offner/material/adhesive/fan description against the present build; record humidity/condensation monitoring and any actually installed mitigation.
9. Separate connector part numbers and installed extension lengths for the identified Omega probes and Labfacility KX extension wire.

# Software and configuration

Status: source inspected on 23 October 2026; normal procedure clarified by the owner on 27 October 2026. No hardware-control program was executed to build this documentation. The owner-confirmed normal settings and the earlier copied source profile are distinguished below. [Owner review R1](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026).

The 33 shared Python/shell files in the supplied local copy were verified against repository commit `df4ccebbbd0f41e32f5ae415e967728e5845d56b` dated 12 October 2026 and matched byte for byte. The additional `Config/local_config.py` was preserved as a [historical snapshot](reference/local_config_snapshot.txt). Its 12 °C pre-cool setting was a deliberate shorter trial; normal pre-cool uses `probe_5` at **5 °C**. Reproducing that old profile and preparing a normal run are different configuration choices. See [source provenance and maintenance](10-sources-and-maintenance.md) and [owner review R1](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026).

## Software layers

The host PC owns sequencing, MCC I/O, wheel movement, temperature logging, data transfer, and analysis. The camera computer owns the V4L2 video device, image-capture pipeline, and internal temperature queries. Camera-side Python modules are deployed separately; editing the local copy does not update the running camera. [Sweep orchestration](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L201), [camera deployment](../Scripts/deploy_camera_scripts.sh#L7).

| File or group | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `Config/system_config.py` | Base host configuration: motion, DIO, network endpoints, control features, test timing, recovery and metadata; imports local overrides at the end. |
| `Config/local_config.py` | Site/run overrides, including the required local results path. The original copied profile is preserved as historical evidence; its trial settings are not the normal protocol. |
| `Config/temperature_config.py` | MCC network endpoint and thermocouple channel definitions; imported directly by the temperature controller. |
| `Config/analysis_config.py` | Filter identities, nominal wavelengths/widths, image ROIs and analysis options; imported directly by analysis. |
| `Control/temperature_control.py` | MCC connection, thermocouple readings, Hall input, lamp/freezer/camera output switching. |
| `Control/temperature_logger.py` | Background nominal 1 s logging, latest-record access and forwarding control methods through one owned controller. |
| `Control/filterwheel_control.py` | Calls `ticcmd`, sets motion/current parameters, moves to positions, Hall homing and shutdown. |
| `Control/camera_keepalive_stream.py` | Starts, checks and stops a remote camera stream to `/dev/null`; captures process/event details. |
| `Scripts/run_long_test.py` | Repeated tests, pre-cool, camera power sequence, stop conditions, scheduled sweeps, storage checks, event/summary files and bounded camera recovery. |
| `Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py` | One wheel sweep, optional homing, illumination timing, internal camera readings, per-filter remote capture, transfer and local presence checks. |
| `Camera_scripts/camera_config.py` | Camera-side video format, resolution, frame rate, default exposure and gain. |
| `Camera_scripts/camera_control.py` | Applies V4L2 settings, runs a one-frame GStreamer PNG pipeline, checks file existence/size, and writes per-image metadata. |
| `Camera_scripts/capture_remote.py` | Camera-side entry point accepting output path and optional exposure-control value. |
| `Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py` | Camera-side JSON readout from `sensors -j` and V4L2, including temporary-stream refresh. |
| `Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py` | Single-test image metrics, temperature columns, CSVs, plots and profile diagnostics. |
| `Scripts/preview_analysis_rois.py` | Image/ROI previews used to review analysis regions. |
| `Scripts/analyze_repeat_tests.py` | Batch single-test analysis, cross-cycle diagnostics and repeatability summaries. |
| `Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit.py` | Interactive comparison application with metadata editing. |
| `Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py` | A second comparison implementation with expanded test/repeat-group browsing. The authoritative entry point needs owner confirmation. |
| `Scripts/repair_repeat_group_metadata.py` and `Scripts/repair_and_rename_repeat_folders.py` | Historical metadata/folder repair tools. They modify stored records or names and are not required for a normal new acquisition. |

The analysis methods and data interpretation belong to the analysis chapter; this chapter records their software entry points and environment requirements.

## Configuration precedence

`Config/system_config.py` defines base values, then performs `from Config.local_config import *` inside an `ImportError` handler. Therefore the supplied local values win for consumers that import from `Config.system_config`. Editing a base value with an existing local override will not change the effective value. [Override mechanism](../Config/system_config.py#L169).

Important boundaries:

- `Config/temperature_config.py` and `Config/analysis_config.py` are separate configurations; the wildcard import does not replace the direct imports from those modules.
- The camera imports `camera_config.py` on the camera computer. Host overrides are not automatically shared with it. The host explicitly passes each filter's exposure value to the camera capture entry point.
- Many constants are imported by value when a program starts. Restart the appropriate process after changing configuration; do not expect live reload.
- `LOCAL_DATA_ROOT` is defined only in the supplied `local_config.py`, although acquisition/preflight import it from `system_config.py`. Removing the local file does not produce a complete working base-only configuration. Its current path refers to a different Linux user's home directory; choose a reviewed, writable results location on the intended host.

Sources: [temperature import](../Control/temperature_control.py#L23), [analysis import](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L13), [camera-side import](../Camera_scripts/capture_remote.py#L4), [explicit exposure transfer](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L319), [local results definition](reference/local_config_snapshot.txt#L5), [host imports](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L15).

## Normal pre-cool and the historical copied profile

For normal operation, the owner specifies cooling until **`probe_5` is at or below 5 °C**, then switching the freezer off before the camera starts. The copied profile's **12 °C** threshold was deliberately chosen for a shorter recent trial. Neither the old base default of −5 °C nor the historical 12 °C trial should be substituted for the normal 5 °C threshold. [Owner review R1](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026), [implemented threshold check](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L383).

The table retains the earlier source profile for provenance. “Base” means the original value before local overrides; “historical copied profile” means the effective values from the preserved local snapshot. Settings in that column describe the copied trial profile, not a standing instruction to reuse every value for future runs. [Base timing and pre-cool settings](../Config/system_config.py#L62), [base endpoint settings](../Config/system_config.py#L119), [historical local overrides](reference/local_config_snapshot.txt#L5).

| Setting | Original base | Historical copied profile | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PRECOOL_BEFORE_TEST_ENABLED` | `True` | `True` | Automated pre-cool before each test. |
| `PRECOOL_SENSOR_NAME` | `probe_2` | `probe_5` | Probe used for the cooling threshold. |
| `PRECOOL_TARGET_C` | -5 °C | 12 °C | Historical shorter trial; normal threshold is 5 °C on `probe_5` (owner review R1). |
| `PRECOOL_TIMEOUT_HOURS` | 4 h | 7 h | Maximum pre-cool wait. |
| `PRECOOL_POLL_INTERVAL_S` | 5 s | 5 s | Threshold polling cadence. |
| `PRECOOL_SETTLE_AFTER_FREEZER_OFF_S` | 60 s | 60 s | Delay after switching freezer off. |
| `TEST_END_MODE` | `time` | `temperature` | Copied profile uses a probe threshold. |
| `TEST_END_SENSOR_NAME` | `probe_2` | `probe_5` | Probe used for measurement endpoint. |
| `TEST_END_TARGET_C` | 40 °C | 40 °C | Measurement threshold. |
| `TEST_END_DIRECTION` | `above` | `above` | Endpoint requires temperature at or above threshold. |
| `TEST_END_REQUIRED_CONSECUTIVE_READS` | 3 | 3 | Several new logger records must satisfy endpoint. |
| `TEST_END_SAFETY_TIMEOUT_HOURS` | 14 h | 14 h | Temperature-mode deadline checked between operations; blocking work and the endpoint sweep can extend wall-clock duration. |
| `TEST_END_FINAL_SWEEP_ENABLED` | `True` | `True` | Immediate final sweep when endpoint/timeout occurs between scheduled sweeps. |
| `TEST_DURATION_HOURS` | 1 h | 12 h | Duration setting for time mode; not the copied temperature-mode endpoint. |
| `SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | 180 s | 120 s | Wait scheduled after each attempt; capture/transfer time adds to start-to-start spacing. |
| `MAX_SWEEPS` | 25 | 500 | Cap on numbered attempts including failures; can terminate before temperature endpoint. |
| `REPEAT_TEST_COUNT` | 1 | 8 | Number requested in the repeat sequence. |
| `REPEAT_DELAY_BETWEEN_TESTS_S` | 0 s | 60 s | Delay between completed tests. |
| `REPEAT_CONTINUE_AFTER_FAILURE` | `False` | `False` | A failed test normally ends the repeat sequence. |
| `REPEAT_STOP_FILE_NAME` | `STOP_REPEAT` | `STOP_REPEAT` | Stop-sequence marker in the local results root. |
| `CAMERA_KEEPALIVE_STREAM_ENABLED` | `False` | `True` | Keep video pipeline active between image sweeps. |

The implemented sequence keeps camera power off during pre-cool, switches the freezer off at the threshold, waits the settle period, and then switches camera power on for the configured 45 s boot wait. There is no camera warm-start feature in the reviewed runner. [Implemented pre-cool](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L330), [implemented power-on](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L559).

### Other control, recovery and timing settings

| Setting group | Current value or behavior | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Camera power control | Enabled; active-high DIO bit 2; 45 s boot wait; end-of-test off flag enabled. | [System settings](../Config/system_config.py#L34) |
| Freezer control | Enabled; active-high DIO bit 3. Duplicate base declarations have the same values. | [System settings](../Config/system_config.py#L51) |
| Lamp capture delay | 2 s after lamp-on; lamp then remains on for the sweep's image loop. | [Setting](../Config/system_config.py#L159), [sequence](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L299) |
| Acquisition retry | 30 s retry delay; maximum consecutive failures 3. | [Settings](../Config/system_config.py#L142) |
| Storage threshold | 5 GiB (`1024**3` bytes per unit) free-space threshold on the local output filesystem. | [Setting](../Config/system_config.py#L146), [check](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L73) |
| Automatic camera recovery | Enabled; up to 3 per test; camera off wait 15 s, then boot wait and keepalive restoration. Triggered by recognized capture-error strings. | [Settings](../Config/system_config.py#L41), [implementation](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L185) |
| Manual freezer diagnostic | Configured on-time 600 s and final off wait 600 s. | [Settings](../Config/system_config.py#L76), [diagnostic](../Scripts/test_freezer_relay.py#L51) |

The 600 s minimum-off constant is used by the manual freezer diagnostic's final wait; it is not a general interlock inside `freezer_on()` and is not imported by the long-test runner. The diagnostic initially waits only 2 s between commanding off and then on. Its name/comment does not establish protection against a compressor that was switched off immediately before the diagnostic. Review the actual freezer requirements and sequencing before interpreting this setting as enforced protection. [Diagnostic initial sequence](../Scripts/test_freezer_relay.py#L80), [low-level freezer output](../Control/temperature_control.py#L116), [runner imports](../Scripts/run_long_test.py#L15).

## Camera capture configuration and behavior

| Camera-side setting | Supplied value |
|---|---|
| Video device | `/dev/video4` |
| Frame size | 1296 × 1032 pixels |
| Pixel format | `GRAY8` |
| Frame rate | 24 frames/s requested |
| Gain | 0 requested |
| Default exposure control | `exposure_time_absolute=20000` |
| Image staging root | `/root/scripts/data` |
| Configured log root | `/root/scripts/logs`; the capture controller shown here does not itself use `LOG_ROOT` |

Source: [camera configuration](../Camera_scripts/camera_config.py#L2).

The host normally overrides exposure per filter: 3000, 15000, 8000 and 15000 for filters 1–4 respectively. A missing mapping uses host `DEFAULT_EXPOSURE_TIME_ABSOLUTE=20000`. The optional CLI argument to `capture_remote.py` takes precedence over the camera-side default. These numbers are driver-control values; unit/range confirmation remains open. [Exposure settings](../Config/system_config.py#L148), [CLI override](../Camera_scripts/capture_remote.py#L16).

Before each frame, the camera program applies requested frame rate, exposure and gain through `v4l2-ctl`, waits 0.1 s, and queries settings. It then runs `gst-launch-1.0 -e` with `v4l2src num-buffers=1`, raw `GRAY8` caps, `pngenc`, and `filesink`. The output is one PNG from an 8-bit grayscale input pipeline, plus a JSON sidecar. This does not establish the sensor's native bit depth or record higher-bit raw samples. [Settings](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L80), [pipeline](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L106).

The sidecar records requested and before/after applied exposure/gain, stream parameters, image dimensions and encoding, capture status, file size, timestamp and the pipeline command. Success requires a nonempty image file. It does not include an image-content/saturation/alignment acceptance check at capture time. The timestamp is recorded before launching the pipeline, not a hardware exposure timestamp. [Capture verification and metadata](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L126).

## Streaming and internal-temperature configuration

The copied local profile enables a long `v4l2-ctl --stream-mmap` stream on `/dev/video4`, with `100000000` requested frames, 2 s startup wait, frames discarded to `/dev/null`, PID file `/tmp/freezertest_keepalive_stream.pid`, and log file `/tmp/freezertest_keepalive_stream.log`. It is finite by frame count, despite being called continuous/keepalive. The code tests process existence for status, not actual frame progress or sensor freshness. [Settings](../Config/system_config.py#L99), [historical local enablement](reference/local_config_snapshot.txt#L36), [status](../Control/camera_keepalive_stream.py#L91), [launch](../Control/camera_keepalive_stream.py#L126).

Normal capture shares the same video node, so the sweep reads internal temperatures while the keepalive is active, stops it, waits 2 s for buffers/device release, captures all filters, then restarts it and reads temperatures again. The sweep avoids starting a second refresh stream if a keepalive object was supplied. [Sweep sequence](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L282).

Keepalive startup can terminate stale matching `v4l2-ctl` streams to `/dev/null`, including streams whose PID file was lost. This is useful cleanup but matters if someone is using another such diagnostic stream on the camera. Stop first requests termination and waits about 3 s, then force-kills if necessary. [Stale cleanup](../Control/camera_keepalive_stream.py#L134), [stop](../Control/camera_keepalive_stream.py#L184).

For reads without keepalive, the temporary sensor-refresh stream requests 300 frames and waits 1 s before reading `sensor_temperature` while the stream remains running. Internal temperature collection is enabled but non-fatal: the sweep retains failure/error details and continues capture. A successful remote JSON read can still contain sensor-specific errors, so inspect `remote_payload.errors` and per-sensor warnings rather than relying on outer `status=success`. [Refresh configuration](../Config/system_config.py#L88), [temporary stream](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L152), [host wrapper](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L81), [combined payload](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L335).

## Dependencies and environment

No requirements manifest, lockfile, or packaged environment was present among the supplied files. The following dependencies are established by imports and external commands; versions and complete installation procedure remain to be recorded from the working test systems.

| Environment | Dependencies used by the supplied source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Host acquisition | Python 3.10+ syntax, `uldaq`, MCC runtime/driver capable of the configured network device, `ticcmd`, OpenSSH `ssh` and `scp` | `str \| None` type hints require Python 3.10 or later in files without postponed annotation evaluation. The correct MCC runtime and permissions depend on the actual installed unit/system. |
| Host preflight | Above, plus `ping`; writable output storage | Includes device connection and output-state changes; not purely passive. |
| Camera computer | Python 3.10+ syntax, `v4l2-ctl`, `gst-launch-1.0`, V4L2 device/driver, GStreamer elements `v4l2src`, raw-video caps, `pngenc`, `filesink` | Camera scripts use standard-library Python modules; actual capture depends on external binaries/plugins. |
| Camera internal readings | `sensors` with JSON output, `v4l2-ctl` | Missing optional hardware-monitor readings are returned as errors. |
| Host offline analysis | NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, Pillow; SciPy for Gaussian fitting | SciPy import failure is caught, but enabled Gaussian fit metrics cannot then be treated as available. |
| Interactive comparison | Streamlit, pandas, Plotly | Two application files exist; confirm which one is maintained. |

Sources: [DAQ imports](../Control/temperature_control.py#L12), [Tic call](../Control/filterwheel_control.py#L42), [SSH](../Scripts/run_single_sweep_remote.py#L51), [capture pipeline](../Camera_scripts/camera_control.py#L114), [hardware-monitor command](../Camera_scripts/read_camera_temperatures.py#L99), [analysis imports and SciPy fallback](../Scripts/analyze_test_folder.py#L4), [dashboard imports](../Scripts/compare_tests_streamlit_updated.py#L31).

Run host commands from the repository root with the project available on the Python import path, as shown by the diagnostic scripts' examples: `PYTHONPATH=. python3 Scripts/<entry_point>.py`. Camera-side files are colocated and import their sibling modules directly. Do not use hardware-control scripts as an automated test suite simply because their names begin with `test_`.

## Deployment and diagnostics

`Scripts/deploy_camera_scripts.sh` copies four camera-side files using SCP and then creates data/log directories over SSH. Its camera endpoint/account are hard-coded inside the shell script rather than read from `Config/system_config.py`; changing the Python endpoint does not update this deployment destination. It copies into `/root/scripts/` **before** creating subdirectories, so `/root/scripts/` must already exist for a first deployment. It does not install dependencies or compare deployed checksums. [Deployment script](../Scripts/deploy_camera_scripts.sh#L4).

| Program | Intended use | Material actions and limitations |
|---|---|---|
| `preflight_check.py` | Connectivity, SSH, camera script/data presence, Tic availability/status, output storage, MCC temperature/Hall read | Creates/deletes a storage test file; MCC connect/disconnect changes outputs and can turn camera off. `--test-camera-capture` creates/deletes a remote capture; `--test-lamp` toggles lamp. It is not suitable to run alongside an active test. |
| `read_temp_loop.py` | Print/log thermocouple readings nominally every second | Uses full `TemperatureController`; connect/disconnect output side effects apply. Writes `temperature_log.jsonl` in working directory. |
| `test_hall_sensor.py` | Watch raw Hall state while manually moving wheel | Standalone hard-coded MCC endpoint, AUXPORT0 bit 1; does not consume the shared host/channel configuration. Runs at top level when executed/imported. |
| `calibrate_filterwheel.py` | Manual wheel alignment and saved position map | Operator verifies/calibrates filter positions before each run because the internal motor reference may drift. Moves/energizes motor and optionally controls lamp/camera; saved JSON is not auto-applied to running configuration. |
| `test_homing_repeatability.py` | Three home cycles with +250 position offset between cycles | Produces diagnostic JSON and temperature log; controller positions are not a calibrated optical repeatability measurement. |
| `test_filterwheel_idle_current.py` | Move each configured filter, wait 10 s for manual idle-current/heating check | Does not perform Hall homing itself; current state/position reference must be understood before motion. |
| `test_freezer_relay.py` | Exercise freezer contactor | Switches real freezer and waits; CLI can override waits. Does not enforce a global minimum-off interlock. |
| `test_camera_internal_temperatures.py` | One remote camera-temperature JSON read | Can create a temporary video stream; not just a file read. |
| `test_capture_with_keepalive_stream.py` | Diagnostic experiment capturing while streaming | Deliberately probes the concurrent-access case that the production sequence normally avoids. |
| `test_keepalive_pause_capture.py` | Exercise pause/capture/restart sequence | Changes streaming state and captures an image; production-like control diagnostic. |

Sources: [preflight main](../Scripts/preflight_check.py#L275), [MCC preflight cleanup](../Scripts/preflight_check.py#L185), [temperature loop](../Scripts/read_temp_loop.py#L19), [standalone Hall watcher](../Scripts/test_hall_sensor.py#L16), [homing diagnostic](../Scripts/test_homing_repeatability.py#L33), [idle-current diagnostic](../Scripts/test_filterwheel_idle_current.py#L38), [freezer diagnostic](../Scripts/test_freezer_relay.py#L51), [internal reading diagnostic](../Scripts/test_camera_internal_temperatures.py#L17), [concurrent-stream experiment](../Scripts/test_capture_with_keepalive_stream.py#L4), [pause/capture diagnostic](../Scripts/test_keepalive_pause_capture.py#L4).

## Configuration review checklist for the next revision

1. Confirm which copied source version matches the running host and deployed camera; record commit/checksums and environment versions.
2. Select the intended local results path and confirm it is writable on the host actually running tests.
3. Confirm current camera identity/operator/notes rather than carrying them into every future run unchanged. Their supplied values describe one configured run context.
4. Check the normal `probe_5` pre-cool threshold of 5 °C; retain deliberate trial departures as explicitly identified run settings.
5. Confirm shared-supply sequencing, actual compressor limits and whether protections should be enforced centrally.
6. Record exposure-control units/range, controller motion units and required current against the actual hardware.
7. Choose the maintained Streamlit entry point; preserve historical repair tools as explicitly manual utilities.
8. Record the approved physical probe map, then keep probe names and end-condition settings aligned with it.
9. Verify/calibrate filter positions before each run and manually focus on the target plane whenever the camera is changed. These are owner-confirmed preparation tasks; preflight does not perform them. [Owner review R1](10-sources-and-maintenance.md#r1-owner-review-27-october-2026), [operating preparation](04-running-the-test.md#operator-preparation).

title: Running the freezer test
